subject: Dedicated capacity carveout + autoscale exception — SummitPilot
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@sumtech.com>, Lucy Ramos <lucy@sumtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SummitPilot capacity ask: carveout + autoscale exception

Team —

Quick summary: SumTech (prospect pilot that went well in PoC) wants a 6–8 week dedicated trial in Q3 (target start 2027-08-01) to validate steady-state latency under real traffic for a customer-facing recommender. They are asking for a short-term dedicated GPU pool plus an autoscale exception so they can burst during two product launch events.

Requirements (from SumTech):
- Baseline throughput: ~18k tokens/sec sustained (peak traffic windows ~30k tokens/sec)
- Model: re-ranked ensemble with a 13B candidate encoder + 7B reranker; running on fp16 / 4-bit quantized where possible
- Preferred hardware: 8x A100-80GB equivalent for the reserved pool; burst to additional 4 GPUs for the two demo days
- Duration: 6–8 weeks (initially request 1 month, with option to extend)

I've attached the pilot requirements spreadsheet.

Ask: can platform provision a temporary carveout and approve an autoscale policy exception (burst allowance) for the two launch dates? Also need a short list of operational guardrails we should require (SLOs, telemetry, rollback).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ops/infra confirms feasibility and exact GPU types + slot counts
2) Product defines QoS & rollback criteria
3) Commercial confirms discount/credits and procurement timeline

Can we get a feasibility note and a proposed config by EOD Monday (2027-05-24)? SumTech is eager to lock dates.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
attachments: summitpilot_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@sumtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitPilot capacity ask: carveout + autoscale exception

Monica — thanks for the summary and the attachment. Quick clarifying questions before we scope:
- Are the 18k / 30k tokens/sec numbers across the whole cluster or per model instance?
- Expected median sequence length and 95th pct? That changes memory and batch size planning.
- Do they need KV/prefix cache between requests (session affinity)?

Operational note: we can provision a temporary dedicated pool and allow controlled burst capacity, but autoscale exceptions require an ops-approved QoS profile and runbook. For initial feasibility I need:
- exact peak windows (dates/times) so we can schedule capacity without impacting other reserved customers
- spike duration and concurrency distribution

Proposed immediate deliverables from infra:
- feasibility doc with GPU type/options (A100-80GB or H100 equivalent), pool size, and estimated cost delta
- recommended autoscale guardrails (max burst GPUs, timeboxed windows, auto-rollback triggers)

I'll take point on the infra feasibility doc and link to INF-2142. Putting a placeholder on my calendar to deliver a first draft by 2027-05-24 EOD.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Director, Platform Operations
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@sumtech.com>, Lucy Ramos <lucy@sumtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitPilot capacity ask: carveout + autoscale exception

Following up with a proposed configuration after reviewing the requirements spreadsheet. High level: feasible with constraints.

Technical proposal (draft):
- Dedicated pool: "summitpilot-usq3" — 8x A100-80GB (reserved)
- Burst lane: allow +4 GPUs for two pre-agreed windows (2 hours each)
- Network and storage: use existing VPC peering + NVMe scratch; increase ephem storage for KV caches by 200GB
- Autoscale exception: timeboxed policy with hard caps; autoscale override requires ops token + alerting to on-call
- QoS & rollback triggers:
  - If p95 latency > 1.2x baseline for > 10 minutes -> immediate throttle to baseline pool size
  - If error rate increases > 3% relative -> auto-fallback to smaller model variant and notify SRE

Operational runbook items:
- Canary ramp: 2 days of 25% traffic, then 2 days at 50%, then full traffic on day 5
- Telemetry: enable per-request token-level latency and cost breakdown; tag metrics with summitpilot_*.

I attached a short PDF with proposed reservation terms and suggested credit level. We should get commercial confirmation on the concession before approving the carveout.

-Karthik
VP, Product
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
attachments: proposed_reservation_terms.pdf (PDF)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Anika Bose <anika@sumtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitPilot capacity ask: carveout + autoscale exception

Thanks Karthik — this looks reasonable as a starting point. A few product / risk points to call out:

- Impact to other reserved customers: we need a mitigation plan if cross-tenant interference is detected. Suggest a strict isolation-enforcement check during the canary window.
- Billing/credits: confirm the discount band and whether SumTech will accept a conditional extension clause (extension only if SLOs/usage meet agreed thresholds).
- Support model: we should provide a named SE for the pilot and a 24/7 response channel for the 48-hour launch window.

Proposed canary schedule (tight):
- 2027-08-01: infra provisions pool
- 2027-08-03–04: canary ramp (25% -> 50%)
- 2027-08-06: demo day 1 (burst window 2hrs)
- 2027-08-20: demo day 2 (burst window 2hrs)

Ben — can you confirm commercial OK on the proposed credit level and whether we can approve the timeboxed burst? If approved, I'll own the isolation checks and the rollback plan.

-Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@sumtech.com>, Lucy Ramos <lucy@sumtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitPilot capacity ask: carveout + autoscale exception

Team — quick commercial confirmation: approved a one-month carveout with a 20% credit off the estimated incremental usage for the pilot period, conditional on procurement signing a short SOW by 2027-07-15. If SumTech wants the full 6–8 weeks we'll re-evaluate extension based on telemetry and SLO adherence.

Next steps (action items):
- Monica: share SOW template with SumTech and loop procurement (due 2027-07-15)
- Dev: finalize infra feasibility and post exact GPU SKU options (due 2027-05-28)
- Marissa: produce isolation runbook and rollback criteria (due 2027-06-02)
- Karthik: finalize reservation terms in INF-2142 and link the doc

Monica — feel free to give SumTech a heads up that commercial is tentatively green; final approval is conditional on the SOW. Good work moving this forward.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
ben_carter@redwood.com
attachments: none
